d0c4141418.q: What is cognitive surrender in AI engineering and why does it kill AI projects?
d0c4141418.a: Cognitive surrender is when you say 'just go do it' without thinking about what the AI is doing or verifying its output. Ethan experienced this when he gave Claude access to all his documentation and code without reviewing anything, resulting in the system using outdated information and strange implementations. He learned that you must spend 30-40% of your time thinking through a project completely to avoid this mistake.

09d09a5308.q: How does building a semantic layer with LookML improve AI accuracy for data queries?
09d09a5308.a: A semantic layer with LookML tells the AI agent where to find data and what calculated metrics are already defined. Instead of Claude trying to figure out how revenue is calculated every time, it already knows through LookML. This prevents the AI from going to wrong projects or datasets and ensures deterministic, accurate responses—Ethan's team achieved 100% accuracy when using this approach versus 70% without it.

397f01d365.q: What is the verification tax problem with AI outputs and how does trust in data prevent it?
397f01d365.a: The verification tax is the second job created by AI—proving that every AI output was correct. If a number is wrong even once, it seeds fear, uncertainty, and doubt in users, who then stop using the system and you have to work twice as hard to regain trust. Ethan solved this by hard-coding authentication to restrict AI access to only three production-level projects, building an MCP server, and incorporating Twyman's Law so Claude verifies itself.

ef2fd40f46.q: How did Google Conversational Analytics help achieve 100% accuracy compared to raw Claude queries?

d9a829d523.q: What step-by-step approach should engineers follow to avoid cognitive surrender in AI projects?
d9a829d523.a: Start with a voice conversation with Claude—an hour-long dialogue where you repeatedly ask 'why' to understand its thinking and expand your own. Keep asking clarifying questions to correct its reasoning, which becomes embedded in how Claude thinks to itself. Once you feel confident about the problem space, move to text and request all requirements in visual form, ensuring you understand the architecture completely before building.
